search_strategy: The agent bulk-dumped every Mattermost channel and every wiki page's comments to local files (/tmp/mm/*.txt, /tmp/wiki2/*.txt) rather than relying on live search -- a sound approach given BookStack does not index comments. It read the two wiki comments that matter (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) in full via `cat /tmp/wiki2/<id>.txt`. For mail it used IMAP to list and filter ~15 candidate files by retry-shaped keywords before opening any, which caught 2 of 3 mail remarks but silently dropped g3.r1.l12 (subject-filtered out). For chat, it built a keyword-matched, deduped, chronologically sorted context file (ctx2.txt, 541 lines) and began reading it in full 40-45 line chunks -- this phase correctly recovered the herring/reversal timeline and most of the r1 waiver-pool remarks. After ~180 lines (~1/3 of the way through, reaching only into March) it judged the file 'noisy' and switched to a narrower single-line keyword grep (ctx3.txt) for everything from April onward, which surfaces one matching chat line per hit with NO surrounding turns -- fine when a remark is a single self-contained line, but fatal for g3.r1.l13, whose payload sits in the reply AFTER the line the keyword matched. It also supplemented with a handful of full-window channel dumps (awk NR-range, sed -n ranges) for specific dates it had flagged as needing follow-up, but never flagged the Apr 24 'invalid api key' thread for expansion, and never returned to finish reading ctx2.txt in full.
end_reason: Not a failed/zero run. The agent completed the open feature (retry_policy.py, wiring, provider de-duplication), merged via PR #737, CI green on 555e4d4, and the release deployed (provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1, g3.suite_ok=1). reward=0.6667 reflects exactly 3 of 9 hidden facts scoring 0: g3.r1.exclusions_or_crossover and g3.r1.observability (both from the same missed TERMINAL-zeroing clue, g3.r1.l13, seen only as a truncated fragment) and g3.r2.rule (missing round(...,3) in remaining_cooldown_seconds, whose sole clue g3.r2.s1c was never surfaced).
